en.body:
Before finding himself fighting for survival in the snow-choked, zombie-infested Raccoon City of the new **Resident Evil** film, **Austin Abrams** was already a familiar face to fans of TV's ultimate zombie-adjacent horror. His turn as Bryan Hodukavich in the 2026 **Resident Evil** movie, where he plays a bumbling medical courier on a perilous last delivery, taps into a well of experience that includes a memorable villainous role on a show that explored the terrifying aftermath of societal collapse.

While details on the specific TV series where Abrams previously played a villain are scarce, the implication is a narrative steeped in the kind of high-stakes, life-or-death scenarios that fans of **Resident Evil** crave. This prior experience likely informed his nuanced performance as Bryan, a character described as "goofy and gormless" but who, under duress, becomes "more and more alive." The film's director, Johannes Roberts, and co-writer Shay Hatton have crafted an original story that pays homage to the beloved video game franchise, placing Abrams at the heart of an outbreak that threatens to consume everything.

## A Familiar Face in the Apocalypse

Abrams' casting in **Resident Evil** is more than just a new lead; it's a nod to his growing presence in genre storytelling. His ability to convey vulnerability and resilience, even in the face of overwhelming odds, is a key asset. In the film, Bryan's journey is a desperate race against time as he navigates the treacherous landscape of Raccoon City, a place synonymous with the genesis of the zombie outbreak in the games. The snowy drive to the hospital, carrying a mysterious package, quickly devolves into a fight for survival against infected monsters, showcasing Abrams' capacity for physical performance and comedic timing amidst genuine terror.

## Stakes and Fan Anticipation

Fans of the **Resident Evil** franchise, known for their deep engagement with its lore and characters, will be keen to see how Abrams' portrayal of Bryan connects with the established universe. The film's critical reception, particularly praise for Abrams' performance, suggests a compelling entry into the long-running saga. The ending, which leaves Bryan's battle seemingly unwinnable and "almost literally hanging," is a clear signal from the filmmakers that they are setting the stage for more, leaving audiences clamoring for a sequel. This deliberate narrative choice amplifies the stakes for Bryan and hints at a larger story yet to unfold within the **Resident Evil** universe.

What's Next

With the **Resident Evil** film now captivating audiences, all eyes are on potential future installments. Details regarding a sequel have not yet been announced, but the film's conclusion strongly suggests the story of Bryan Hodukavich is far from over.

content_raw: Getting trapped in the world of Resident Evil is no fun for anyone - luckily, Austin Abrams has a fair bit of experience dealing with zombies.
